description:
## Surah Al-Inshiqaq - The Rending Asunder

(Revealed at Mecca)

25 Verses in 1 Section

**Sections of Surah Al-Inshiqaq**

1. The Day of Reckoning.

In the name of God the Beneficent the Merciful

Sunnat Sajdah – Prostration Recommended

translations.1: When the heaven shall rend asunder (Refer to: <{["Q", "82:1"]}>.)
translations.2: And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and (as) it ought to do!
translations.3: And when the earth shall be stretched out (flattened) (Refer to: <{["Q", "71:26"]}> or disintegrated.)
translations.4: And shall cast forth whatever is in it and becometh empty (Refer to: <{["Q", "99:1"]}> - <{["Q", "99:2"]}>.)
translations.5: And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and as it aught to do!
translations.6: O' man! Verily thou art in strive unto thy Lord, (with) a striving, and thus thou art meeting Him!
translations.7: And he who is given his Book in his right hand. (Refer to: <{["Q", "17:71"]}>, <{["Q", "69:19"]}>.)
translations.8: Soon shall he be reckoned (with) an easy reckoning
translations.9: And he shall return unto his people delighted
translations.10: And he who is given his Book (from) behind (Left Side, Refer to: <{["Q", "69:25"]}>.) his back
translations.12: And shall be committed to the flaming fire
translations.13: Verily he was joyous (In his life in the world before death.) among his people
translations.14: Verily he thought that never will he return (unto God)
translations.15: Yea! Verily his Lord was always vigilant of him
translations.16: And I swear by the Glow of the sunset" (84:61)
translations.17: And (by) the night and what it enshroudeth
translations.18: And (by) the moon when at her full
translations.19: That ye shall certainly march (Ride.) from state to state
translations.20: But what then hath happened unto them that they believe not?
translations.21: And when is recited unto them the Qur'an, they prostrate not in obeisance (Refer to: <{["Q", "7:206"]}>, <{["Q", "13:15"]}>, <{["Q", "22:77"]}>, <{["Q", "32:15"]}>.) ?
translations.22: Nay! those who disbelieve belie (the Truth)
translations.23: And Verily God knoweth best what they hide (in their hearts)
translations.24: So announce thou unto them the tidings of a painful chastisement!
translations.25: Save those who believe and do good deeds, for them shall be a recompense unending (Refer to: <{["Q", "41:8"]}>.)

exegesis.1: Refers to what will happen to the sky at the dawn of the Day of Judgment, i.e., when the sky will be rent asunder - to manifest the state of reality.
exegesis.2: The heavens with their greatness, and limitless extent, only await the command of the Lord which shall be carried out.
exegesis.3: The earth will be changed from its global form to a flat levelled plain.
exegesis.4:
All the things - minerals, metals and the bodies of the innumerable generations buried in it, i.e., all its contents, will be thrown out, i.e., the earth will vanish with all its contents destroyed, and reduced to nothing.

In this verse and <{["Q", "99:2"]}> points out the time for the disintegration, i.e., when the earth's productive capacity gets exhausted, and this principle is applicable to all growing and evolutionary movement in every part and particle of the Universe. (A.P.)
exegesis.6: The path of righteousness, i.e., the path of those who earnestly wish to get nearer to the Lord, is full of toil and misery. It is the godly ones that scorn and forego the pleasures of this life and choose the life of want and difficulties. Those who toil in the sincere hope of meeting the Lord, are assured of their success so that they may not fall victims to dejection and give up their quest for Him.
exegesis.7: Those who suffered, and yet led pure lives of faith and righteousness and suffered miseries in the way of the Lord <{["F", 1]}>and yet toiled continuously to earn His pleasure for which they avoided the pleasures of this life and chose for themselves and remained contented with the miseries and sufferings. They avoided evil in spite of its strong attractions and earned goodness at all costs.
exegesis.8:
The reckoning will be affected without the least difficulty. The Holy Prophet said that he who has these three qualities shall meet a very easy accounting at the judgment. He said: -

1. To provide the one who hath deprived thee of the legitimate due.
2. Meet the one who shuns you.
3. Pardon him who has been unkind to you.
exegesis.9: To his people, i.e., to his kith and kin and the others spiritually on the same level with him without the restriction of the age, i.e., preceding or succeeding him in time.
exegesis.10: The disbelievers and the wicked will have their hands tied at their back and hence they will be given their records from behind them. He would wish that he had not been given any record at all<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.11: The wicked would wish for death and annihilation once for all but they will be in a state which will be neither life nor death<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.13: While in this life the wicked one was happy rejoicing and enjoying the pleasures of the world among his people, i.e., relatives and friends, without any regard to the pleasure or the displeasure of the Lord.
exegesis.14: Man is led into the evil ways of life mostly of his self-complacence and self-conceit and getting himself intoxicated of the enjoyment of his carnal desires in his lower life, forgetting his personal responsibility and his accountability on his return to the Lord in the ultimate. He must remember the inevitability of his return to Him.
exegesis.15: Man forgets that the Lord is ever watchful of him for his motives as well as his deeds.
exegesis.16:
The beautiful and wonderful show of the radiance of the sun in the evening which is the work of nature.

The note on this verse by a commentator<{["F", 1]}> is another example of a wishful distortion of the Qur'an narrowing its original significance to the rise and the fall of the Arabs in power. (A.P.)
exegesis.17: Man's attention is drawn to the mystic functioning of the great and the wonderful phenomena of nature in the daily life in this world, the functioning of the wonderful organization of the universe being before man's eyes all the while he takes these great events of the life, to be so common and so easy that he does not think of ever pondering over the secret of the genetic factors in the functions of nature which every moment passes from one stage or state into another or regulated and controlled that the daily repetition is maintained with perfect success without the least failure.
exegesis.20: With so much of the guidance from heaven through the wonderful manifestation of the Might, and the Wisdom and the Existence of God and so much of the exertion to bring home to man the Truth, through a long line of God's inspired men, His apostles, if man still fails to believe in the reality, it is naturally a matter of wonder and surprise.
exegesis.21: The Prostration means respect, reverence and the humble submission to God<{["F", 1]}> - Prostration on the part of the reciters of this verse is only '_Sunnat'_, traditional, and not '_Wajib'_, i.e., compulsory.
exegesis.22: It is said that when above verse 21 was revealed, the Holy Prophet went into prostration and the believers present there followed his example. The disbelievers got over the backs of the believers lying in prostration and standing on the heads began clapping their hands. It was then these verses were revealed.
